newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia Petco awards Malacca naphtha term tender.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Petco awards Malacca naphtha term tender.

text.p: Petco, trading arm of Malaysian state-owned oil firm Petronas has awarded a nine-month term tender to sell naphtha from its Malacca refinery but is not awarding cargoes from Kertih, a company source said on Thursday.

"We have awarded the term tender to sell naphtha from Malacca," the source said. But he declined to reveal the premium at which the contract was awarded for the sale of 50,000 tonnes of naphtha per month between January and September 1997.
"The price is in line with the market for 1997," he said.

Traders said that current spot premiums for naphtha from Malacca, where Petronas operates a 100,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery, are at around $1.00 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
Petco awarded its 1996 term naphtha sale tender at a premium of about 5 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes on an fob basis. But this time the premium was believed to be substantially larger.
The source said there was no award for cargoes to be lifted from the 50,000-bpd Kertih refinery as "all the cargoes have already been committed for export."
